LLM Index for Scientific Computing

Generated 2026-11-17 · 111 models scored in the default view from 278 measured by Artificial Analysis · raw cost data only

Full ranking

Two benchmark sets and two Omniscience modes. The default uses all nine benchmarks with separate accuracy and non-hallucination components (ten total). The science subset has seven; combined Net Score replaces the two rates with one, giving nine and six components respectively. Each view uses its own complete cohort. JavaScript lets the benchmark, Omniscience and sort controls work independently. Bold rows are that view's Pareto frontier members. In cost view, models with no published cost data sort last.

All nine benchmarksScience subset Ten-component SoftMinZ over the full v5 suite. Seven-component SoftMinZ over the science battery.

Each point is a model: vertical position is the ten-component SoftMinZ performance index, horizontal position the raw cost of one agentic task (log scale). The dashed line is the Pareto frontier — models for which no cheaper model is at least as good. Frontier members are colour- and shape-coded; everything else is grey.

What SoftMinZ measures

SoftMinZ standardizes each component across one complete cohort and takes a nonlinear soft-minimum in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0. Two benchmark sets are each available in two Omniscience modes. The default all-benchmarks, separate-rates view has ten components from nine benchmarks; the science subset, separate-rates view has seven components from six. Combined Net Score replaces the two rates with one component in either set.

Default: all nine benchmarks, separate rates (ten components)

  • Terminal-Bench 4.0
  • FrontierCode 2.0
  • AA-Omniscience v1.1 — Accuracy
  • AA-Omniscience v1.1 — Non-hallucination
  • HLE-Diamond
  • CritPt v2 (Hard Subset)
  • Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1
  • AA-Briefcase v1.1
  • AutomationBench-AA
  • GDP.pdf

AA-Briefcase v1.1 contributes its Elo-style rating; AutomationBench-AA its partial score; GDP.pdf its all-pass rate. AA-Omniscience v1.1 contributes two distinct inputs: accuracy and non-hallucination rate (1 minus AA’s hallucination rate). Each of the ten components gets its own cohort mean, sample standard deviation and z-score.

A model must have a finite score on all ten components to receive the all-benchmarks SoftMinZ or contribute to any of its normalization pools. Partial profiles are excluded from both the ranking and all z-score pools. Every component uses the same complete cohort of 111 models, with its mean and sample standard deviation:

zb = (xb − μb) / sb   ;   sb uses the n − 1 denominator
Z = Σi=1…10 exp(−zi)
SoftMinZ = −ln(Z / 10)

Terminal-Bench 4.0 measures general terminal execution; FrontierCode 2.0 tests changes to real software repositories; Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 covers scientific terminal workflows. CritPt v2's hard subset and HLE-Diamond test difficult scientific reasoning and knowledge. AA-Omniscience v1.1 contributes accuracy and non-hallucination rate as separate components.

A model must have a finite score on all seven components to receive the science-subset SoftMinZ. Same strict complete-cohort rule, same sample standard deviations:

Z = Σi=1…7 exp(−zi)
SoftMinZ = −ln(Z / 7)

Complete cohort, sample z-scores

The partition function is divided by the component count to take the mean of the Boltzmann factors, not a linear average of the z-scores. AA's Intelligence Index weights do not weight either performance score. A component's local influence is exp(−zi) / Z, so weaker components matter more; there are no fixed linear score weights. The soft-minimum lies between a model's worst and mean z-score. Weak dimensions receive more influence: balanced excellence is rewarded, while strength on one benchmark cannot linearly cancel weakness on another.

Combined mode scores AA-Omniscience v1.1 — Net Score (combined), the published −100 to 100 metric, in place of both separate rates. Combined all-benchmarks and science views have nine and six components. Each of the four views has an independently computed complete cohort and normalization; scores across modes are not directly comparable. The former SciCode, AA-LCR, original HLE and original CritPt measurements are not used. FrontierCode 1.x, full CritPt v2 and AA-Omniscience v1 cannot substitute for the named versions or hard subset. Versions are not treated as interchangeable.

The battery, evaluation versions and cohort changed with AA v5.0. These values and rankings are not directly comparable with either the former pre-v5 battery or the initial six-component v5 score that used the combined Omniscience Index. Missing data is never filled with older benchmark versions.

In separate mode, Omniscience accuracy and non-hallucination are used directly as separate rates, not reconstructed from the combined Index. In combined mode, the published Net Score is used instead. Briefcase Elo and the AutomationBench-AA and GDP.pdf rates enter as published. If the cohort is too small or any required spread is zero, generation aborts rather than computing a partial-dimension index.

Cost per expensive agentic task

The cost axis is a separate workload selection from the science performance battery. We retain the original technique: read AA's published weighted per-benchmark cost per task, divide by that benchmark's current Intelligence Index weight, and average the unweighted costs using task counts.

The four selected workloads are AA-Briefcase v1.1, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1. They are the clear high-cost, long-running agentic-workload group in the v5 published data. This is a fixed set for every model, not a model-specific choice of whichever measurements look favorable.

Cb = weightedCostPerTaskb / wb
Ctask = Σb∈cost subset Cb Tb / Σb∈cost subset Tb

Today's denominator is 359 tasks across those four workloads. Task counts and weights are parsed from AA's live methodology table. Repeats are not multiplied into the task counts: the input is AA's published per-task cost, not the cost of our rerunning its evaluations.

AA-Omniscience v1.1 and HLE-Diamond have many cheap questions and do not enter the cost average. GDP.pdf, AutomationBench-AA and CritPt v2 (Hard Subset) are also excluded from this cost subset because their typical published per-task costs are substantially lower than the four selected workloads. A benchmark can be included in performance without being included in cost, and vice versa. GDPval-AA and AA-LCR are no longer members of the v5 Intelligence Index and supply no cost weights here.

All nine current Intelligence Index cost components, including the excluded cheap ones, must be present in a cost split and must sum to AA's published total before the four-workload cost is accepted. Costs are never inferred from token prices, a related model or another reasoning level. Only 100 of 111 scored models have a complete positive published cost today; the remainder show — and are excluded from the log-cost chart and Pareto frontier, not treated as free. Source-zero prices are also excluded rather than promoted as zero-cost winners. A zero in one published component is retained if the complete four-workload average is positive. AA’s reported costs retain its published cache-hit and pricing assumptions; they are not cache-free estimates.

How this differs from AA's Intelligence Index v5.0

AA's v5.0 index covers Knowledge Work, Coding, Science and General, at 25% each. Its weights and task counts, parsed for this run, are shown below. AA-Omniscience's 15% share comprises 10% accuracy and 5% non-hallucination. In separate mode SoftMinZ uses the two measured rates as independently standardized components, but does not copy AA’s 2:1 performance weighting; in combined mode it uses the published Net Score. In either mode every component enters the normalized partition sum once.

We use AA's weights only to undo its cost weighting. Our performance index uses sample z-scores across a strict complete cohort and a nonlinear soft-minimum, rather than AA's weighted average of normalized evaluation scores. The default battery covers the same nine benchmarks as the Intelligence Index; the science-subset view narrows to the six benchmarks most relevant to scientific computing.

Reproducibility

Scraped scores are cross-checked against overlapping scores on each evaluation page, using JSON-LD score rows when available and the evaluation-page model payload otherwise. A benchmark whose parsed values disagree is rejected rather than published; missing comparison data is reported as unavailable, never as validated, and aborts generation. Intelligence Index weights and task counts used in the cost model are parsed live from the AA methodology page on every run (today: live (AA v5.0 methodology page, parsed this run)); if that page is unreachable or its table cannot be parsed, the run aborts rather than publish costs computed from stale weights.
